newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says China silenced dissent.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says China silenced dissent.

text.p: The United States on Thursday accused China of effectively silencing in 1996 all public dissent against the communist party and the government.
In its annual human rights report, the State Department concluded that "no dissidents were known to be active at year's end."

"The Chinese government in 1996 continued to commit widespread and well-documented human rights abuses, in violation of internationally-accepted norms, stemming from the authorities' intolerance of dissent, fear of unrest and the continuing absence of laws protecting basic freedoms," the report said.
"All public dissent against party and government was effectively silenced by intimidation, exile or the imposition of prison terms, administrative detention or house arrest," it said.

The United States regularly criticises China's record in its annual assessment of human rights around the world. This year's hard-hitting report comes as Washington and Beijing have been making a major effort to improve their relationship, which had deteriorated seriously. This year's report would seem to make it impossible for the United States not to sponsor a controversial resolution at the U.N. Human Rights Commission in Geneva faulting China's record.
